title: Baa, Baa, Black Sheep - A Classic Sing-Along for Toddlers
description: Three bags full! Sing and clap along with this gentle farmyard favourite. #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #farmsong
characters: Three adorable Black toddlers: Zuri, a 3-year-old girl with deep warm brown skin, round afro puffs tied with soft yellow fabric scrunchies, wearing a sunny yellow t-shirt, denim dungaree shorts and white sneakers; Kofi, a 4-year-old boy with medium-deep brown skin, short dark natural curly hair, wearing a blue t-shirt, grey jogger shorts and red sneakers; and Nala, a 3-year-old girl with deep brown skin, neat cornrow braids, wearing a yellow pinafore dress over a white t-shirt, white tights and pink sneakers

lines: Baa, baa, black sheep, have you any wool?
Yes, sir, yes, sir, three bags full
verses.scene: A round woolly black sheep stands in a sunny green meadow beside a low stone wall, with two toddlers looking on.

lines: One for the master, one for the dame
One for the boy who knows my name
verses.scene: Three fat sacks of soft wool sit on the grass; Kofi lifts one and grins as Nala counts them on her fingers.

lines: Clap your hands and sing with me
Baa, baa, black sheep, one, two, three
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together in the meadow, counting to three with big smiles.

lines: Baa, baa, black sheep, soft and warm
verses.scene: The sheep skips in a happy circle around a small red barn while the toddlers cheer it on.

lines: Clap your hands and sing with me
Baa, baa, black sheep, one, two, three
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together in the meadow, counting to three with big smiles.

pd_source.author: Traditional (English)
pd_source.publication: Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book, vol. II (London, c. 1744) — the earliest surviving printing.
pd_source.public_domain: Anonymous traditional text first printed c. 1744; nearly three centuries old and long out of copyright everywhere.
pd_source.adaptation: Verse 1 is the traditional text verbatim. In verse 2 the closing line 'One for the little boy who lives down the lane' is shortened and re-rhymed to 'One for the boy who knows my name' to fit the 9-word line limit and to give the verse a clean rhyme. Verse 3 and the hook are NEWLY WRITTEN in the same meter.

song_style: children's nursery rhyme, cheerful upbeat kids song, cute female child voice, simple very repetitive catchy melody, gentle bouncy tempo, playful, bright, warm
